/kind bug
/sig node
/priority critical-urgent

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Avoids overwriting statuses or phase on terminated pods.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--

_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #105358

#### Special notes for your reviewer 

Passing a bool around is ugly, but checking `kl.podWorkers.IsPodKnownTerminated(pod.UID)` is expensive, and we don't need to by the time we invoke `syncTerminatedPod`.

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

When a pod is evicted under resource pressure, it goes into an error state.

#### What you expected to happen:

The pod terminates normally.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Note that the 130GB file is based on **90% of total disk space - current utilization** to hit the default eviction threshold.

kind: Pod
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: evictme
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10
  containers:
  - name: busybox
    image: k8s.gcr.io/e2e-test-images/nginx:1.14-2
    command: ["sh", "-c", "fallocate -l 130G file; sleep 100000"]

ehashman@fedora:~/src/k8s$ cluster/kubectl.sh get pod
No resources found in default namespace.

ehashman@fedora:~/src/k8s$ cluster/kubectl.sh apply -f ~/tmp/disk-pressure.yml 
pod/evictme created

ehashman@fedora:~/src/k8s$ cluster/kubectl.sh get pod

ehashman@fedora:~/src/k8s$ cluster/kubectl.sh get pod

Confirmed that this is a regression from 1.21. When running the reproducer against the release-1.21 branch, the pod above correctly stays in Evicted status (since pods are mortal). On 1.22, it tries to restart, entering either an Error or ContainerCreating state.

/kind regression

Roughly, kubelet syncTerminatingPod sends "Failed" to status manager (which looks like it generates the correct apiserver patch for phase running -> failed), then somehow by the time Kubelet syncTerminatedPod is called it sends "Running but with errors" to status manager, and status manager allows that transition (internally) and then sends it to the apiserver.  So the pod goes Running -> Failed -> Running which should never happen (we "lost" that the pod was stopped).

Bug 1: pod patch status probably shouldn't allow terminal -> nonterminal phase transitions (didn't we fix that??)
Bug 2: pod worker is supposed to be getting most up to date status from status manager before calling syncTerminatedPod, which should include "Failed", but that isn't happening? thus the status manager then sends a "non-terminal state" (shouldn't ever happen)

Roughly, figure out why status passed to syncTerminatedPod is older than what was sent by syncTerminatingPod, then figure out why status manager allowed that transition back to running, then figure out why apiserver didn't reject.

Staring at logs, I've figured out where the illegal phase transition is happening:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/38746752af6d0ec955f4511a727da37347da3b92/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1831-L1838

Thus, I feel like syncTerminatingPod must have the bug: it returns successfully, but the containers of the pod aren't all actually terminated.

The containers ARE terminated, we just haven't retrieved their status.  This is because of a decision to not refresh the container status cache in syncTerminatingPods.  So syncTerminatingPod is not a bug.

So then perhaps the right thing to do here would be to refresh the container status cache before syncing another status to the API server in `syncTerminatedPod`? Then we can avoid syncing the outdated cached status https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/38746752af6d0ec955f4511a727da37347da3b92/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1835-L1838

Updating from an internal discussion last night - bug 2 isn't actually a bug.  Lantau convinced me we wouldn't refresh the status cache, so what happens is we call generatedAPIStatus with:

1. older API status (mostly irrelevant)
2. freshest status manager status
3. up to date container cache (but 2s) after

The key thing is that phase from runtime status is irrelevant when 1 or 2 are terminal - because runtime has no idea about whether a pod is terminal.  So roughly we should be ignoring phase from 3 except when determining when to go from pending to running.  The bug here is that we're thinking that this is an "illegal transition" but still copying the latest reason and message (runtime status doesn't get to weigh in on overal terminal phases).

We shouldn't need to refresh status at all.

Elana identified the issue on status here - previously we NEVER reported container status after an eviction, so the refactor (which correctly ensured container exit codes showed up) was returning containers with state=waiting,lastState=terminated, which is incorrect.

generateAPIStatus needs to know the difference between "current container status, waiting for more to show up" and "any status we have is the best we have".  So once killPods succeeds in syncTerminatingPods and in syncTerminatedPods, we're no longer "waiting".  So generating pod status should correctly summarize the container status as `state=terminated` and not inject `state=waiting`.
